questions.q: In sys.database_files, what does is_percent_growth = 0 mean about the growth column?
options: growth is a fixed number of 8 KB pages, not a percentage
The file will never autogrow
growth represents a percentage of the log file only
The file has reached its maximum size
questions.explain: When is_percent_growth is 0, growth is expressed in 8 KB pages; when it's 1, growth is a percentage of current file size.

questions.q: Why is percentage-based autogrowth considered an anti-pattern on a large file?
options: The size of each growth event increases as the file grows, turning into large unpredictable I/O spikes
Percentage growth is not actually supported by SQL Server
It only affects tempdb, never user databases
It causes CHECKDB to report false consistency errors
questions.explain: A 10% growth on a 500 GB file adds 50 GB in a single event, versus 1 GB on a 10 GB file — the same percentage compounds into an increasingly disruptive event.

questions.q: Why does percentage-based autogrowth on a busy transaction log file cause visible transaction stalls?
options: Log growth events are serialized — no other log activity proceeds while the log is growing
It causes the database to automatically go into SINGLE_USER mode
It triggers a full DBCC CHECKDB run automatically
It disables the transaction log entirely during growth
questions.explain: Log file growth blocks other log activity until it completes, so a large percentage-driven growth event directly stalls transactions.

questions.q: Which query returns file growth settings for every database on the instance, not just the current one?
options: SELECT ... FROM sys.master_files
SELECT ... FROM sys.database_files
DBCC CHECKDB WITH NO_INFOMSGS
SELECT ... FROM sys.dm_exec_query_stats
questions.explain: sys.master_files is instance-wide and queryable from any database, unlike sys.database_files which only describes the current database.

questions.q: What is the recommended fix for percentage-based autogrowth, per this lesson?
options: Set a fixed-size FILEGROWTH increment and pre-size files to their expected working size
Disable autogrowth entirely with no fallback
Switch the database to the SIMPLE recovery model
Increase the percentage to grow faster and reduce the number of events
questions.explain: A deliberate fixed increment (e.g. FILEGROWTH = 512MB) produces predictable growth events regardless of file size, with autogrowth acting only as a safety net.
